questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, what should the driver do?

options.text: Inspect the vehicle first, then compare their notes with the report.
Review the report first when starting an inspection.
Skip the pre-trip inspection and only use the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review the report first when starting an inspection.
questions.explanation: Start a vehicle inspection by reviewing any report left by the previous driver.

questions.question: What is an acceptable oil pressure when the engine is running?
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should be between 35 and 75 psi when running. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or unstable.

questions.question: If stopped on the side of the road, the driver should:
questions.explanation: If stopped on the roadside, turn on four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.question: What does ABS allow you to do?
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheels from locking up during hard braking. Drive and brake the same way with or without ABS.

questions.question: Black ice is usually very thick.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, making it look like wet pavement.

questions.question: When approaching a vehicle for pre-trip inspection, why should you look under it?

options.text: To check if the vehicle is on an incline.
To check for fresh fluid leaks.
To check if it is in a parking spot.
To check if the vehicle is on a decline.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check for fresh fluid leaks.
questions.explanation: Look under the vehicle for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks on the ground. Leaks mean there is a problem that must be fixed before driving.

questions.question: During pre-trip inspection, what is a sign of trouble?
questions.explanation: Check under the vehicle for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks. These indicate a problem that must be repaired before driving.

questions.question: Which is a sign of a possibly drunk driver?
questions.explanation: Warning signs of impaired driving include trouble staying in lane, trouble keeping a steady speed, or stopping for no clear reason.

questions.question: How many identical placards must be on a vehicle carrying hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Hazardous material placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: Is it normal to find fresh oil under a vehicle?
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check under the vehicle for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks. Leaks indicate a problem that must be fixed.

questions.question: You should not smoke within ____ of a vehicle carrying Class 3 or Division 2.1 materials.
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a vehicle carrying Class 3 (flammable liquids) or Division 2.1 (gases) materials. Do not smoke or carry a lit cigar, cigarette, or pipe within 25 feet of any vehicle carrying Class 1 (explosives), Class 4 (flammable solids), or Class 4.2 (spontaneously combustible) materials.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is a look?

options.text: Checking the gauges on the instrument panel.
Getting out of your seat and walking to the back of the vehicle to check its position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Getting out of your seat and walking to the back of the vehicle to check its position.
questions.explanation: A look happens when you open your door, leave your seat, and walk to the back of the vehicle to check its position. During straight line backing, you can use only one look. During other exercises, you can use up to two looks.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Only if you think there might be a problem.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving. This helps you stay aware of traffic and watch for problems with your vehicle.

questions.question: If your coolant level is low, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Check your oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid when inspecting your engine. In all weather, your engine needs enough coolant to run properly.

questions.question: Before driving in winter, you should check:
questions.explanation: Before winter driving, check your heating and defrosting equipment, coolant and antifreeze levels, wipers and washers, tire tread, tire chains, lights, reflectors, and exhaust system. Clear ice and snow from all windows, mirrors, handholds, steps, deck plates, and radiator shutters. Make sure the winterfront is not closed too tightly.

questions.question: When driving down a hill, your vehicle's speed will likely:

options.text: Match the speed of other traffic.

questions.explanation: Gravity causes your vehicle to speed up on a downhill slope. Before going downhill, choose a safe speed based on your vehicle's size and weight.

questions.question: If your brakes fail on a long downhill slope, you should:

options.text: Turn the vehicle off and then back on to reset the brakes.
Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downhill slope, use an escape ramp if available. If there is no escape ramp, look for another escape route, such as a side road or open field.

questions.question: A registered vehicle should have:

options.text: A mirror on the left side only.
Mirrors on both the left and right sides.
A mirror on the right side only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mirrors on both the left and right sides.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires knowing what is happening on all sides of your vehicle. Your vehicle should have mirrors on both sides, and you should check them regularly.

questions.question: When turning, when should you turn off your turn signal?

options.text: In the middle of the turn.

questions.explanation: When turning or changing lanes, signal early and keep signaling the whole time. Turn off your signal after you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: When backing, using another person to help guide you is not recommended.
questions.explanation: When backing, it is always a good idea to use a helper to watch your blind spots.

questions.question: What is a Class 7 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Class 7 hazardous materials are radioactive materials.

questions.question: In hot weather, tar bleeding spots on the pavement are:

options.text: Just as safe as the rest of the road
Safer than the rest of the road

questions.explanation: In hot weather, tar rises to the road surface and becomes very slippery. Watch for these spots and be careful.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:

options.text: The tires need to be replaced

questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts means the nuts are loose. Check them before you drive.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of bad brake drums or shoes?

options.text: Shoes without brake fluid on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes without brake fluid on them
questions.explanation: Bad brake signs include cracked drums, pads or shoes with oil or brake fluid on them, and worn or broken shoes. Shoes without brake fluid on them are normal.

questions.question: After driving over a bridge during the driving test, you may be asked to recall:

options.text: The color of a sign you passed
How many traffic lanes were on the bridge
Whether there was a crosswalk on the bridge

questions.explanation: During the driving test, the examiner may ask you to remember the weight limit posted on a bridge you crossed.

questions.question: In an emergency, you should:
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest choice in an emergency. It is usually safer to steer away from danger to avoid a crash.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: Vehicles behind a truck:

options.text: May have difficulty seeing ahead of the truck
Usually have a clear view of the road ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: May have difficulty seeing ahead of the truck
questions.explanation: A truck can block the view of drivers behind it. Warn them by flashing your brakes before you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include difficulty focusing, repeated yawning, daydreaming, and drifting out of your lane. Being able to focus is not a sign of fatigue.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter a truck's cab because of:

options.text: Not enough oil in the engine

questions.explanation: A damaged exhaust system is dangerous because poisonous fumes can enter the cab.
